rationale: Extensive cohort analysis and case series of biallelic NOTCH3 disease consistently establish a clear radiological dichotomy between biallelic loss-of-function (LoF) variants and biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants. In a comprehensive analysis of 50 biallelic cases (Iruzubieta et al., 2024), all 26 individuals with biallelic LoF variants demonstrated a distinctive neurodevelopmental pattern characterized by periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, with recurrent confirmation across independent reports (Stellingwerff et al., 2022; Tasharrofi et al., 2024; Ouskri et al., 2025) explicitly highlighting the sparing of anterior temporal poles. In contrast, biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients in Iruzubieta et al.) manifest the classical CADASIL neuroimaging spectrum, marked by confluent white matter hyperintensities characteristically involving the anterior temporal lobes and external capsules without early periatrial volume loss.

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) caused childhood-onset stroke and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) presented with a CADASIL spectrum phenotype including deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

evidence.text: Patients harboring biallelic cysteine-sparing/loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants exhibited extensive white matter changes, atrophy, and basal ganglia lacunes with explicit sparing of the anterior temporal lobes.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: MRI findings pointed at a small vessel disease, with extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, atrophy, lacunes in the basal ganglia, microbleeds, and microcalcifications. The anterior temporal lobes were spared.

evidence.text: A proband with a homozygous null NOTCH3 variant presented with severe early-onset neurological features and diffuse MRI white matter abnormalities with notable absence of anterior temporal pole involvement.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed on a proband who exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions.

evidence.text: A 12-year-old Moroccan girl with a homozygous frameshift loss-of-function NOTCH3 mutation displayed bilateral periventricular white matter lesions rather than anterior temporal pole predilection.

source.title: A novel homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant in a Moroccan patient: expanding the spectrum beyond CADASIL
source.quote: We report a 12-year-old Moroccan girl, born to first-degree consanguineous parents, presenting with global developmental delay, spastic tetraparesis, epilepsy, and bilateral periventricular white matter abnormalities.

new_directions.question_text: Does MRI quantitative volumetry of the periatrial white matter versus anterior temporal pole differentiate atypical non-cysteine missense variants from true null/frameshift NOTCH3 mutations?
new_directions.rationale: Recent reports have described homozygous cysteine-sparing missense variants with temporal pole hyperintensities (e.g. Luo et al., 2026), indicating a need to systematically determine whether non-cysteine missense variants act biochemically as loss-of-function or retain dominant-like arteriopathic properties.
